summary: Saint-Léonard Airport (YSL) is a regional airport serving the town of Saint-Léonard in Madawaska County, northwestern New Brunswick, near the Canada–United States border with Maine. It functions primarily as a general aviation facility supporting the surrounding francophone community and regional travel needs. The airport provides an important aviation link for this remote part of the province where ground transportation options to larger centers are limited.
faqs:
Q: What is Saint-Léonard Airport primarily used for?
A: It serves mainly general aviation, private flights, and regional connectivity for the Madawaska region of New Brunswick.

Q: Are there commercial passenger flights at YSL?
A: No scheduled commercial passenger service operates at Saint-Léonard Airport; it is used for private and charter aviation.

Q: Where is the airport located relative to the town?
A: The airport is situated on the outskirts of Saint-Léonard, a short drive from the town center in northwestern New Brunswick.

Q: What nearby larger airports are available for commercial travel?
A: Travellers can use larger airports in northern Maine or drive to Fredericton or Moncton for broader flight options.
transport_tips: A personal vehicle is the most practical way to reach Saint-Léonard Airport, as public transit options in this rural region are limited. The airport is easily accessed by local roads connecting Saint-Léonard to the Trans-Canada Highway (Route 2). For travellers without a car, arranging a rental vehicle or taxi service in advance from Edmundston or Saint-Léonard is recommended.
local_tip: If planning a visit, note that Saint-Léonard sits in New Brunswick's bilingual Madawaska region—many locals speak French as their first language, so a few French phrases go a long way with staff and residents.
